children.innerHTML: We built a room around a fire, then spent seven years learning to listen to it.
There is no gas line into the building. Every dish that leaves the pass has been touched by the same oak fire, lit at three in the afternoon and read like a barometer until close.

attributes.alt: Elias Voss on the line before service

children.innerHTML: Elias cooked in kitchens with brigades of forty and menus that never changed. Ember is the opposite of that: one room, five cooks, a menu written in pencil. He spent a year building the hearth before serving a single plate, and still calls the fire the head chef.
His rule for the kitchen is borrowed from his grandmother's farmhouse stove: if the fire is wrong, nothing else can be right. Cooks here learn wood before they learn knives.
Lit the same way every day, read differently every day. We cook to the fire we have, not the one we planned for.
The menu follows the market, not the other way round. When the trout is done for the year, so are we.
Most of what we serve was started days ago. The fire does not hurry, and neither does the room.

meta_description: The room, the hearth and the cook: how Ember came to cook everything over one oak fire.
